title: Tressfecta wants to make hair braiding a less arduous task for hairstylists
snippet: Tressfecta builds products for textured hair. Its first project is a tool called Plait Pilot that helps braiders with the initial process of separating hair from packs before braiding begins.
fullText:
Aisata Diallo, 24, calls herself a lifelong braider. “I’ve always braided my hair growing up and, at some point in my college career, started braiding other people’s hair,” she said. At Northeastern University in Boston, she found limited access to braiders and textured-hair specialists, so she decided to fill that gap by starting a small business of her own. 

“Throughout that experience, I was very close to some of the pain points in the styling process and complained about it constantly,” she said. Braiding is a manual task, and a single style can take eight hours to complete. Many professionals deal with issues like cramping and carpal tunnel syndrome after spending long days standing behind a chair weaving hair into patterns.

At first, Diallo said she didn’t know what to do about it. “I stopped braiding, and one of the reasons that I stopped braiding was due to the physical toll it has on your body.” She wanted to find a way to make braiding less painful and wondered whether new AI technology could automate some part of the process. Building hardware for braiding is expensive, difficult, and complex, which is one reason there have been few innovations in this space. The textured hair market has also long been overlooked by the mainstream.

Image Credits:Aisata Diallo

Then, last year, she had an idea: Tressfecta, a company building products for textured hair. Its first project is a tool called Plait Pilot that helps braiders with the initial process of separating hair from packs before braiding begins. That process alone can take hours, especially when a client wants small braids. Diallo said the device is designed to work like this: A stylist places the braiding hair on top of it and sets the size they want the hair separated into, and the device separates the pieces and dispenses them back to the stylist so they can grab them while braiding. 

“It’s very challenging to build this kind of tool in this space,” she said, citing the nuance and complexity of the braiding style process. Different types of textured hair also need to be accounted for, especially when length and density are considered. “It’s not a one-size-fits-all solution.” 

Tressfecta is still technically prelaunch, and it is working on the prototype of Plait Pilot. Diallo has been bootstrapping the company, while also drawing on funding from grant and accelerator programs. “I am preparing to fundraise,” she said, noting how hard it can be to raise money for hardware, especially beauty hardware. For now, Diallo said she’s connecting with stylists and braiders who can test the technology. She also spent this week in San Francisco as one of TechCrunch’s Startup Battlefield 200 companies. 

She doesn’t remember exactly where she first heard about TechCrunch Disrupt, possibly on LinkedIn or in a founder resource group, but when we talked ahead of the show, which wrapped up on Thursday, she was looking forward to connecting with people and showing off her product. She was especially excited to connect with people and for others to see her product. “It feels like a great opportunity,” she said.

title: Apple confirms Siri AI is not coming to the original HomePod mini
snippet: Siri AI is a tentpole addition to HomePod mini 2, but a CNET report today originally claimed Siri AI was coming to older HomePod mini models too. However, the story has since been updated with a correction and 9to5Mac received a statement confirming Siri AI will be exclusive to HomePod mini 2. more…
fullText:
Siri AI is a tentpole addition to HomePod mini 2, but a CNET report today originally claimed Siri AI was coming to older HomePod mini models too. However, the story has since been updated with a correction and 9to5Mac received a statement confirming Siri AI will be exclusive to HomePod mini 2.

Apple says Siri AI will be exclusive to HomePod mini 2

Earlier today, CNET published a report saying that Siri AI is coming to the older HomePod mini. It originally claimed: “the current S5-powered HomePod Mini will also get Siri AI compatibility later this year, along with updates to iOS 27.2.”

This news seemed unlikely given there’s no evidence on Apple’s website or press releases of HomePod mini 1 supporting Siri AI. Add to this, Apple did explicitly say that Siri AI will come to certain older Apple TV 4K models, and included no such assurance for HomePod mini owners.

CNET ultimately updated its article with a correction saying that Siri AI won’t come to older HomePods. This aligns with what Apple told 9to5Mac.

	

Apple confirmed to 9to5Mac that Siri AI will only be available on HomePod mini 2 as well as Apple TV 4K (2nd generation or later).

The first HomePod mini debuted six years ago, so this isn’t surprising news. The S5 chip is very dated for AI tasks, as evidenced by Apple Watch models requiring much newer chips for Siri AI support.

Would Siri AI support change your HomePod mini 2 upgrade decision? Let us know in the comments.

title: Veritas expands its anti-counterfeit chip to jewelry, trophies, and fragrance bottles
snippet: Counterfeiters are getting better at replicating brands' marks and passing off dupes, known as "superfakes," as genuine items. A startup called Veritas wants to tackle the problem with its own chip that verifies goods.
fullText:
Counterfeits of luxury goods are a major problem for fashion houses. Counterfeiters are getting better at replicating brands’ marks and passing off dupes, known as “superfakes,” as genuine items. A startup called Veritas wants to tackle the problem with its own chip that verifies goods.

Veritas was founded by Luci Holland, a former Tesla technical product manager who also has a background in design and art. Its chip is built to be easily inserted into products without damaging them. Brands can use it to verify whether a product is the real deal, and customers can show a certificate of ownership through the company’s app.

Holland said other approaches are easier to defeat, because a digital record can be reproduced through a copied QR code or static NFC link.

“Our approach combines secure, authenticated chip responses with integration into the product itself. Our chip generates a secure response with each tap and includes a tamper-detection wire. We make the connection between the object and its digital identity part of the proof,” Holland said.

The Veritas founder told TechCrunch over email that the company has just introduced the second version of its chip, which works on metal surfaces and can be scanned through glass.

“The next-generation chip is ready for production and supports a broader range of applications, including jewelry, trophies, hard-surface products, and glass objects such as fragrance bottles,” Holland said. “Alongside our garment integrations, this gives brands more ways to incorporate authentication directly into their products.”

This week, the startup announced a partnership with ATHLOS, a women’s track-and-field competition founded by Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian, who is also an investor in Veritas. As part of the partnership, all 18 championship crowns will include Veritas’ chips so they can be verified.

Image Credits:Veritas x ATHLOS

The company also embedded a chip into a pair of LeBron James’ first Nike shoes, reimagined by artist Adam Port. Tapping a phone to the shoe brings up its history and story.

The company has so far raised $1.75 million in pre-seed funding led by Ohanian’s venture firm Seven Seven Six, with participation from DoorDash co-founder Stanley Tang; Gloria Zhu, co-founder of skincare brand Reys; and former TechCrunch editor Josh Constine.

Since its February fundraise, the company has shipped an iOS app for consumers and a brand portal that lets companies manage product records and build owner experiences. Through the app and the portal, brands can offer experiences such as clubs, event check-ins, and segmented early access to product drops.

Veritas competed in this year’s TechCrunch Disrupt Startup Battlefield, which ran Tuesday through Thursday. A winner was announced Thursday afternoon.

title: IDC: Apple closes in on Samsung as global smartphone shipments see record decline in Q3
snippet: In a report published today, IDC says Apple saw a 4% year-over-year decline in global iPhone shipments during Q3 2026, but its share of worldwide smartphone shipments increased 23.1% over the same period last year. Here’s why. more…
fullText:
In a report published today, IDC says Apple saw a 4% year-over-year decline in global iPhone shipments during Q3 2026, but its share of worldwide smartphone shipments increased 23.1% over the same period last year. Here’s why.

Preliminary data in line with recent downward trend reports

IDC says its preliminary data on global smartphone shipments for Q3 2026 show a 22% drop compared to Q3 2025, which is in line with other regional and global trends reported recently.

The culprit, as even occasional 9to5Mac readers are likely well aware by now, is the ongoing memory shortage, which has sent component costs soaring and squeezed device manufacturers, particularly those competing in lower-end markets.

According to IDC, Samsung remained atop the ranking with 57.8 million units shipped and a 22.6% share, down 5.8% from the year-ago period. Apple came in second with 57.3 million shipped units, followed by Xiaomi, OPPO, and vivo.

The report shows OPPO seeing the biggest drop among the top five, with shipments down 34.5% year over year, and Apple recording the smallest decline at 4%. This left Apple just 500,000 units behind Samsung, with a gap of only 0.2 percentage points in shipment share.

Commenting on these numbers, Nabila Popal, IDC’s senior research director for Worldwide Devices, said things might get worse before they get better:

“The sharp downturn the industry has been bracing for finally materialized in the third quarter this year, with shipments declining a record 22% YoY. However, the worst is yet to come. […] Current indicators suggest that the market has not yet reached the bottom. Memory costs have surged approximately 350% since last year and are still rising, creating substantial pressure on vendor margins and shipments. While memory inflation is beginning to slow down, with a low double-digit sequential increase in Q3 compared to roughly 50%-100% sequential growth in prior quarters, costs remain elevated across other critical components as well, compounding the crunch.”

Today’s report came just two days after IDC released preliminary results for the Chinese smartphone market, where Apple’s share of shipments increased from 15.8% to 17.8%, despite a 4.3% year-over-year decline in iPhone shipments.

snippet: Actor and angel investor Mark Wahlberg says he's OK with using AI in filmmaking, provided it's used "to enhance what you're doing."
fullText:
Even as Hollywood remains divided over the use of AI in filmmaking, actor and director Mark Wahlberg believes the technology has a place in the industry as long as it’s used the right way. 

Wahlberg, who’s also an entrepreneur and angel investor, took the stage at TechCrunch Disrupt to share his perspective on AI’s role in filmmaking, and how he’s open to having an AI likeness of himself carry on his legacy.

The actor said he plans to potentially use AI to enhance certain aspects of the upcoming Pete Rose biopic, in which he’ll star in the title role. 

“It’s a fairly expensive movie, but, we’re talking about utilizing [AI] to enhance the stadium setting, things of that nature,” Wahlberg said. “I don’t think you should just, you know, put an idea into ChatGPT and it puts out a script, and then you should go make that and not use real actors. But if you can use it to enhance what you’re doing, I’m all for that.”

That said, Wahlberg made special mention of his belief that storytelling should remain at the heart of filmmaking.

Image Credits:Kimberly White/Getty Images for TechCrunch

“I’ve done big, effects-driven movies,” Wahlberg said. “I think I was in that kind of sweet spot when the first Jurassic Park was made, or when Perfect Storm came out, and you had that wave, the 100-foot wave that was in the trailer. Those are cutting-edge moments in technology with computer-generated images. Now, I think it’s hard to do that, so I’m not so passionate about effects-driven movies per se, as opposed to real storytelling.”

When asked by TechCrunch Editor-in-Chief Connie Loizos whether he had visited the CAA Vault, a Creative Artists Agency facility which lets actors use scanning technology to capture their bodies, faces, movements, and voices to create AI replicas, Wahlberg said he hadn’t, but would be open to the idea.

“I would be interested because I think in the future, if that’s where things go, it would be cool that my children or my grandchildren could be in charge of my likeness and my image, and hopefully put me in some good movies,” Wahlberg said. “It’ll be interesting to see where things go.”

He even said he wouldn’t be opposed if his upcoming animated series, “Ted,” continued for decades with an AI version of his likeness.

“I think it’s cool if I’m no longer able to do it or don’t exist, and if it could continue and people want to see it, I think it’d be interesting to see where things go,” Wahlberg said. “I think there’s certain things from my childhood that I wish still existed and were still a part of my life […] I wouldn’t be opposed to it. I think people are going to have massive opportunities to watch whatever it is they want, and if there’s a real audience for that, they should be entitled to have what they want to see.”

title: Samsung is now rolling out Android 17 to these older Galaxy devices in the US
snippet: Samsung’s One UI 9 update is now available for the Galaxy S24 and Z Fold/Flip 6, a month after the official rollout was initiated. more…
fullText:
Samsung’s One UI 9 update is now available for the Galaxy S24 and Z Fold/Flip 6, a month after the official rollout was initiated.

Samsung announced that One UI 9 is officially rolling out to devices that didn’t launch with it preloaded – i.e., the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Fold 8 Ultra.

That means the Galaxy S24 series, Galaxy Z Fold 6, and Galaxy Z Flip 6 are the next to get Android 17 (via SamMobile). Of course, the rollout includes all three Galaxy S24 models. The update should appear in the settings app on those devices as a standard download.

For the time being, the update appears to be available in South Korea and the US, though it’s expected that more regions will follow within the next few days.

	

The Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Flip 8 were the first to get One UI 9 because Samsung switched up its update schedule a year ago. A month ago, the Galaxy S26 was given access to the new One UI 9, based on Android 17.

The update has been trickling down Samsung’s Galaxy S lineups ever since. Since the Galaxy S24 and Galaxy Z Fold 6 are just getting One UI 9, it’s expected that the Galaxy S25 and Galaxy Z Fold 5 aren’t far behind. Samsung has not updated those devices just yet.

One UI 9 includes a few notable changes, including:

My FanCam: Automatic video tracking & reframing of a subject

Generative and Editable Cards on Now Brief

Warranty and Care details in Settings menu

More Galaxy AI features: Now Nudge, Creative Studio, Interpreter, Document Scan, Voice Recorder

Privacy & security features: Security Brief, Privacy Alerts, Scam Detection

If the update isn’t ready for you yet, it should be very soon. For those on older devices, it may take a few more weeks.

title: Google updates Android earthquake alerts with more info, expands to 200+ regions
snippet: Google is delivering an update to Android’s earthquake alerts system that will show more information while also expanding support to over 200 regions across the globe. more…
fullText:
Google is delivering an update to Android’s earthquake alerts system that will show more information while also expanding support to over 200 regions across the globe.

Launched in 2021, Android’s earthquake alerts system uses the sensors in Android smartphones to detect the earliest signs of an earthquake and provide a precious few seconds of warning prior to destructive impacts. While the system has had a couple of mishaps, it has also saved lives and Google says it has sent over a billion alerts. 

Effective today, the Android earthquake alerts system is now live in more than 200 regions across the globe, up from 98 previously. Google specifically calls out Panama and Guatemala as new additions. 

Beyond the regional expansion, Google is also updating the design of earthquake alerts. Specifically, the “Be Ready” step is going to offer more information on the location of the earthquake’s epicenter and the estimated magnitude.

	

Google says:

Be Aware: A straightforward alert for estimated light shaking, letting you know an earthquake has been detected nearby.

Be Ready: A detailed alert for stronger shaking, alerting you to prepare to take action.

Take Action: A full-screen alert for moderate to heavy shaking, giving you immediate advice on how to stay safe.

We’ve built-out our Be Ready alert with new helpful guidance. In the coming months, you’ll see a map with a radius of where we’ve detected shaking, estimated earthquake magnitude, action you can take, and a button to learn more about the earthquake as information comes in.

title: Rocket Money’s Rowan is a financial AI assistant you’ll actually want to text
snippet: We have all watched AI assistants become a permanent fixture on our phones over the last few months, yet finding...
fullText:
We have all watched AI assistants become a permanent fixture on our phones over the last few months, yet finding one that genuinely takes everyday chores off your plate is still surprisingly rare. Most general-purpose AI chatbots are great if you want to brainstorm ideas or summarize an article, but they hit a wall when it comes to practical, real-world tasks like managing your personal finances. 

You can describe a theoretical budget to a standard chatbot and get plenty of generic feedback, yet that chatbot cannot keep an eye on your live accounts, start a bill negotiation, or cancel a subscription for you.

That gap between talking and doing is exactly why Rocket Money built Rowan. Designed as an AI-powered personal financial assistant that lives right in your text messages, Rowan proactively watches your money, looks after your budgeting and finances, and does the actual legwork to help save you money so you don’t have to.

When evaluating any new AI tool, the biggest question is what happens behind the scenes after you send a prompt. Most AI assistants can only talk about your money, whereas Rowan is directly connected to your finances and built to take action.

	

Just as importantly, Rowan isn’t a standalone experiment from a brand-new company trying to figure out personal finance on the fly. Rowan has Rocket Money behind it, meaning it runs on the exact same platform that more than 10 million members already use every day. When you ask Rowan to help lower a bill or drop a recurring service, it taps directly into the established subscription cancelation and bill negotiation operations that Rocket Money has been running for years.

It also brings that capability to you without asking you to build a brand-new habit. Because Rowan lives entirely in your text messages, there is no new app to download and no complicated interface to learn. Rowan doesn’t replace the main Rocket Money mobile app, either; instead, it serves as an additional, conversational way to use Rocket Money straight from the messaging inbox you already check throughout the day.

A proactive partner that reaches out first

Most personal finance tools are passive by design, waiting silently on your phone until you remember to open them up and dig through your recent activity. Rowan flips that dynamic by reaching out to you first whenever something in your accounts needs your attention.

On a regular basis, Rowan texts you a weekly spending summary that provides updates on your recent finances and budgeting, complete with a detailed breakdown of where your money went and a heads-up on any areas of concern. In between those weekly check-ins, Rowan keeps a close watch on your day-to-day activity. It texts you automatically when an account balance is getting low, alerts you the moment a new subscription is detected on your statements, and lets you know when prices are increasing on your existing recurring bills.

Because it lives in your texts, checking in on your money becomes a natural two-way conversation. Whenever a question pops into your head, you can text Rowan to get instant financial updates. You can quickly categorize recent transactions right through text, ask about cancelable subscriptions you might want to clear out, or ask how much money is genuinely safe to spend right now based on your current income and upcoming expenses.

Offload financial chores with a quick text

Getting an alert about a price increase or a forgotten subscription is helpful, but Rowan’s real value shows up when you ask it to take things off your plate. Rowan can start work on your behalf so that the only thing you have to do is send a text.

If you spot a recurring service you no longer want, you can simply text Rowan to cancel that subscription. If a monthly service bill is creeping upward, you can text Rowan to start a bill negotiation on your behalf. Of course, because canceling subscriptions and negotiating bills requires coordinating with providers behind the scenes, these actions don’t happen instantly. Rather, your text kicks off the workflow so Rocket Money can step in and handle the follow-through for you. For everyday organization, you can even text Rowan to set a financial reminder, such as asking it to remind you to pay your credit card on the 15th, keeping your monthly routine on track without cluttering up your calendar.

Pricing and how to get Rowan

Available to users in the United States, the core Rocket Money app is free to download and comes with free basic features, including balance alerts, subscription management, spend tracking, basic budgeting, and bill negotiation. To unlock everything the standard app can do for your finances, you can upgrade to Rocket Money Premium, which uses a “pay what you think is fair” approach currently set between $7 and $14 a month.

Rowan is not part of the free app or the standard Premium tier. To get access to Rowan, you will need to subscribe to Rocket Money Premium+, a separate plan available for a flat $15 per month. Upgrading to Premium+ gives you everything included in Rocket Money Premium, plus full access to Rowan right in your text messages.

title: XREAL 1 Pro+ has exactly the right hardware upgrades at the same $599 price
snippet: Ahead of its Android XR-based Aura launching later this year, XREAL is giving its flagship One Pro a “Plus” upgrade without raising the price. more…
fullText:
Ahead of its Android XR-based Aura launching later this year, XREAL is giving its flagship One Pro a “Plus” upgrade without raising the price.

XREAL 1 Pro+ delivers upgrades that, after my experience with the existing generation, are exactly what I would have picked as pain points to address. 

That starts with the display itself. XREAL is nearly doubling the brightness of the display to 1,200 nits as well as introducing AI-powered HDR. While the 700-nit brightness of the older model was plenty bright in dark environments, I did find that it had trouble holding up, say, if my neighbors on a flight decided to have the window open. The 1,200 nit upgrade should go a long way there, and I’m already impressed in some brief testing at home.

The display gets dedicated “Standard,” “Movie,” and “Reading” modes, too, to tailor the display to what the user is doing. 3D conversion also now supports 60Hz, up from the previous 30Hz limit. 

	

The biggest physical upgrade is to the nose pads, which now have a larger air cushion design that, in practice, is a major improvement in regards to wearability. XREAL One Pro often got a bit uncomfortable on my nose after a few hours, but this upgrade makes it a whole lot better. 

XREAL 1 Pro+ is available starting today for $599, keeping the same price as the existing model.

title: Apple just closed the day above $5 trillion for the first time
snippet: Apple today became the second company ever to close with a market valuation north of $5 trillion, following NVIDIA’s landmark achievement in October 2025. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple today became the second company ever to close with a market valuation north of $5 trillion, following NVIDIA’s landmark achievement in October 2025. Here are the details.

Apple counters tech selloff

Apple’s stock closed at $342.96 today, up 0.5% on the Nasdaq. Although modest, the gain was enough to push the company’s market capitalization past the $5 trillion threshold, ending the day at $5.01 trillion.

Today’s result was particularly notable as most of the tech sector operated in the red, with Oracle closing down 8.83%, Meta down 3.27%, Nvidia down 3.16%, Microsoft down 1.8%, Amazon down 1.74%, and Google down 1.68%, to name a few.

Although Apple closed above the $5 trillion mark for the first time, this was not the first time it had reached that valuation. As The WSJ noted, today marked the seventh time Apple crossed the $5 trillion threshold during intraday trading, but the first time it managed to stay above it through the closing bell.

Apple’s stock performance on October 14, 2026

During intraday trading, Apple’s stock reached $347.07 per share, just 0.31% below its record high of $348.15.

Today’s milestone comes on the heels of a series of major product announcements from Apple, including the iPhone 18 Pro lineup, the iPhone Duo, and, just yesterday, the new Apple HomeView, HomePod mini 2, and Apple TV 4K.

It also comes ahead of the company’s fiscal fourth-quarter earnings report on November 2, which will offer a clearer picture of how Apple has navigated rising component costs and the impact of its recent hardware price increases.

Be that as it may, Apple has seen its stock rise roughly 5% since John Ternus took over as CEO on September 1 (or 8.2% if you count the August 31 closing price of $316.85), with today’s milestone further underscoring investor confidence in the company under its new leadership.

title: Google Home bug turns your smart home device list into a mess
snippet: A bug in the Google Home app has left device lists messy for some users, with no obvious way to fix it for the time being. more…
fullText:
A bug in the Google Home app has left device lists messy for some users, with no obvious way to fix it for the time being.

Over the past week, a number of users have run into a problem in the Google Home app that turns the device list into nothing but clutter. 

The way the Google Home app’s “All Devices” page is supposed to work is by grouping linked devices into their assigned rooms, and then show anything that’s not assigned in a room to a generic “Linked to you” section.

That section is the problem right now. Users have found for roughly a week, and we’re seeing the same behavior, that Google Home is listing all of their devices under the “Linked to you” section, whether they’re assigned to a room or not, resulting in a bunch of extra clutter and making it nearly impossible to track down any devices you hadn’t assigned to rooms.

	

“Linked to you” isn’t supposed to include devices already in your room groups
	

This is almost certainly a bug and not an intentional change, but there seems to be no way to fix it at this point, as devices in the list still show their assigned room groupings in the settings menu.

Meanwhile, Google has so far only acknowledged the issue in recommending that affected users reach out to support. 

New Google Home app updates tend to roll out every few weeks, so it’s very possible a patch will clean up this mess sometime soon. Let us know in the comments if you’re running into this problem.

title: Samsung has updated these Galaxy devices to Android 17
snippet: Samsung is now rolling out its Android 17-based update, One UI 9, to its collection of supported Galaxy smartphones and tablets. Here’s the full list of devices that have been updated so far, and what you should know about the update. more…
fullText:
Samsung is now rolling out its Android 17-based update, One UI 9, to its collection of supported Galaxy smartphones and tablets. Here’s the full list of devices that have been updated so far, and what you should know about the update.

What’s new in Android 17 on Samsung Galaxy?

One UI 9, Samsung’s Android 17 update, continues the trend of evolution more than overhaul. The update introduces some slight design tweaks, more AI-powered features, and other changes built on the redesign that debuted in One UI 7 and was iterated in last year’s Android 16-based One UI 8. 

Some key changes in One UI 9 include:

Warranty & Samsung Care status in the Settings menu

Broader support for Now Nudge

My FanCam automatic video cropping based on a select subject

More Quick Panel (quick settings) customization

AI privacy alerts

Upgrades to Samsung DeX

New lock screen clocks that can adapt to your wallpaper

Samsung Galaxy devices with Android 17 – The full list

While Samsung hasn’t confirmed an exact schedule for its One UI 9 and Android 17 rollout for Galaxy devices, there are updates now rolling out in parts of the globe. Below you’ll find a regularly-updated list of every Samsung Galaxy device that has received a stable Android 17 update so far.

	

Galaxy S devices with Android 17

Galaxy S26

Galaxy S26+

Galaxy S26 Ultra

Galaxy S25 (rolling out more widely)

Galaxy S25+ (rolling out more widely)

Galaxy S25 Ultra (rolling out more widely)

Galaxy S25 FE (limited availability)

Galaxy S25 Edge (limited availability)

Galaxy S24 (limited availability)

Galaxy S24+ (limited availability)

Galaxy S24 Ultra (limited availability)

Galaxy Z devices with Android 17

Galaxy Z Fold 7 (limited availability)

Galaxy Z Flip 7 (limited availability)

Galaxy Z Flip 7 FE (limited availability)

Galaxy Z TriFold (limited availability)

Galaxy Z Fold 6 (limited availability)

Galaxy Z Flip 6 (limited availability)

Galaxy A devices with Android 17

Galaxy A57 (limited availability)

Updating…

One UI 9 changelog

Here’s the full changelog from Samsung for One UI 9, as listed for the Galaxy S26 series. Some features may vary by device.

Galaxy AI

Enhanced Now nudge

Now nudge provides helpful suggestions in more places throughout your Galaxy experience. In addition to the keyboard, suggestions will now appear in conversation notifications and in a floating button in the bottom right corner of the screen. There are also several new types of suggestions, like entering reservation details or addresses and saving places in Google Maps.

Focus on someone important

My FanCam lets you select a person in a video and follow them automatically while cropping out the rest of the video.

Interpreter keeps your conversation in front of you

In conversation mode, you can scroll through the whole conversation while you’re still talking.

See useful information during calls

See relevant events and other information related to your current call on the call screen.

Productivity and multitasking

More customizable quick panel

You can now rearrange and customize the controls in your quick panel even more than before. You can change the size of the brightness and volume sliders as well as the media player. You can also separate the sound mode button from the volume slider.

Privacy, security, and device protection

Warranty and care

The new Warranty and care menu in settings lets you check your warranty information and access diagnostic checks and useful information for keeping your Galaxy in top condition.

Lock down your phone quickly

It’s now easier to securely lock your phone in a hurry. Just press and hold the Volume down and Side buttons at the same time or tap the Power button in the quick panel. This prevents biometrics from being used the next time you unlock your phone.

Location access transparency

Stay on top of your location privacy. A blue indicator will appear at the top of the screen when an app accesses your location. Tap the indicator in the quick panel to see which app it is.

Stronger security and privacy protection

Alerts will appear in your Now brief to let you know about risks from malware, apps from unknown sources, unnecessary permissions, and other issues that may put your security and privacy at risk. Apps that have been identified as malicious or vulnerable will be blocked from opening until you make a decision about whether to remove them.

AI privacy alerts

Get help protecting your personal data. AI will monitor how apps use permissions and notify you about unnecessary access to your personal data.

Samsung Health

New look for Samsung Health

Samsung Health has been redesigned to make your health data easier to understand. Enjoy clearer visuals, improved charts, and a more engaging experience to help you reach your health goals.

Customize your Health home screen

Resize cards and organize them by category, like Activity, Sleep, Mindfulness, and Nutrition, so your top priorities are easy to access.

Log health data quickly

It’s now easier to add your health information right from the Samsung Health home screen. You can log your mood, meals, and more. You can even use the camera for faster input.

Advanced trend analysis

Track your progress with improved trend charts in Samsung Health. View data in hourly, daily, or weekly intervals, pinch to zoom in for a closer look, and overlay multiple charts to compare your performance across different periods.

Monitor changes in your sleep vitals

Samsung Health helps you notice meaningful changes in your sleep health data. Use Galaxy Watch or Ring measurements to better understand your daily health patterns.

Manage your heart health

Track key health metrics and lifestyle factors that affect your heart. A daily score based on your sleep, exercise, BMI, and blood pressure helps you better understand your current heart health trends.

Track your cardio load

See how your workouts and activity impact your heart so you’ll know when to push harder and when to rest. Your target cardio load range adjusts daily based on your recent activity and training focus.

Check your fitness index

Your Fitness Index is an overall score calculated using five key fitness metrics: body composition, cardio, strength, flexibility, and endurance. Set a goal and unlock personalized insights tailored to your results.

Keep your ears safe

The new Hearing tracker monitors sound levels detected by your Galaxy Watch and headphone audio levels to help you manage your exposure to loud sounds.

View your cycle and body rhythm

Get a more personalized view of your cycle and body rhythm with new cycle tracking options. You can view your cycle information in your calendar and better understand your health patterns.

Bixby

Activate Bixby with a gesture

Talk to Bixby just by raising your phone close to your mouth and speaking. No wake-up word needed.

Manage your conversations

Keep your chats organized. Search them, rename them, or pin your favorites. You can also delete all of your past conversations at once.

Bixby on the Home screen

Add a Bixby widget to type or talk to Bixby or jump directly to your conversation history.

Accessibility

Discover new Accessibility features

Check the What’s new menu in Accessibility settings to learn about and try the latest Accessibility features for your Galaxy.

Text spotlight for easier reading

Need a closer look? Tap any text on the screen to show it enlarged and highlighted in its own window. You can also customize the font size, colors, and other settings to match your preferences.

Physical keyboard shortcuts

Use shortcuts on your physical keyboard to access the Accessibility settings you need without touching the screen.

Mouse keys enhancements

New options are available when using your keyboard for mouse interactions including speed and acceleration control. You can also use the keyboard’s number pad to point and click.

Replace swipe with single tap

The Replace swipe with single tap option is now located in the Dexterity and interaction menu instead of the Assistant menu for easier access.

Select to speak

Get quick audio readouts without turning on full TalkBack. With the new Select to speak feature, you can select an item on your screen, like text or an image, and hear it read or described out loud.

Improved TalkBack updates

TalkBack updates can now be applied with a simple app update from the Play Store, helping you get the latest accessibility features and enhancements.

Even more improvements

New Lock screen clock

The default clock on your Lock screen has been redesigned with a cleaner and more modern look that adapts to match your wallpaper.

Samsung DeX enhancements

It’s easier to move an app window from one desktop to another using the menu at the top of the window. Desktop previews are now available at the top of the Recents screen, making it easier to switch with a single tap.

fullText:
Hi, friends! Welcome to Installer No. 148, your guide to the best and Verge-iest stuff in the world. (If you’re new here, welcome, hope you’re enjoying all your pumpkin-flavored everything, and also you can read all the old editions at the Installer homepage.)

This week, I’ve been reading about Marc Andreessen and the future of math and Mike Tomlin and Citizens United, reminiscing about the heyday of MySpace, sending this article to everyone as an apology for my bad texting, listening to the Pet Shop Boys’ new Alan Turing album and Dwarkesh Patel’s thoughts on AI, barely keeping myself from preordering an iPhone Duo, asking a lot of questions about that “flying” Tesla Roadster, and endlessly shopping for tripods to hold my phone for social videos. I have thought way too much about tripods this week.

I also have for you a couple of huge new tech docs and a whole bunch of gadgets worth a look. Gadget season, baby! Let’s go.

(As always, the best part of Installer is your ideas and tips. What are you watching / reading / listening to / playing / throwing in the trunk this week? Tell me everything: installer@theverge.com. And if you know someone else who might enjoy Installer, forward it to them and tell them to subscribe here.)

The Drop

You Can See Everything. I can’t remember the last time I was so excited about a documentary (especially a three-hour one). The pairing of Elizabeth Holmes and Nathan Fielder, the shocking level of access, the incredible meta-ness of the whole project. I’ll be seeing this the first minute I can. Oh, and after you watch the doc, watch Josh Johnson’s hourlong set on all things Elizabeth Holmes. Glorious.

Musk. And here’s four more hours of tech doc! The reviews here are also spectacular, and even if you’ve been following the news the last decade or so, I suspect seeing it all in a row at once is going to be an experience.

The Apple HomeView. I keep staring at the buy button on this new $299 home hub. I’m not sure what I need it for, really — my very basic smart home is working just fine — but there’s something almost old-school about the idea of this as a sort of family computer. I’m certainly in the market for fewer reasons to look at my phone.

The new Siri Remote. I cannot in good conscience recommend a $300 Apple TV, but I can totally tell you to drop $60 on the new Find My-enabled remote! I mean, wait until you lose your existing one first. But you will. These remotes are impossible.

The Fairphone Fairbuds 2. I’ve come to like both Fairphone’s minimalist aesthetic and its emphasis on repairability, and the fact that it gets both into a lighter, smaller, longer-lasting, cheaper-than-AirPods package is pretty exciting.

The Xbox Nano Controller. Look at this little guy! A pocket-sized game controller comes in handy more often than you think (makes the waiting room a lot more fun), and this one has all the buttons you’d expect for Xbox and other games. If the battery life is good, this one’s gonna be a winner.

The Fitbit Edge. I’ve been using a Fitbit Air for a while, and I like it a lot, but I do miss having a fitness tracker that also told me the time. This one does that, plus a little more workout and biometric tracking. It’s not the handsomest wristwear I’ve ever seen, but it is very Fitbit.

The CMF Speaker S. I am a sucker for a cool Bluetooth speaker, and these futuristic milk carton-looking devices are fabulous. I bought one of the small ones immediately, and I’m already debating a second to build out the stereo pair. More companies should make speakers that look good!

E Ink Kaleido 4. This isn’t so much a specific gadget as it is good news for a whole category of gadgets: We have a new version of the color E Ink panel found in lots of devices, with promises of both better colors and better performance. Kaleido has let down a lot of devices, but I’m excited to see what comes of this.

I’ve been reading Kevin Roose’s new book, The AGI Chronicles, this week, and I truly cannot recommend it enough. We sometimes make fun of Kevin for loving (and being loved by) AI too much, but this book is fabulously reported, has taught me a ton, and makes so many things about the AI industry make a lot more sense.

And Kevin’s not done! He and (friend of Installer) Casey Newton are getting ready to launch their new show, Machine Gods, sometime next week. (If you were a Hard Fork fan, you’re gonna need to be listening to this one.) So I figured now was a good time to see how Kevin gets it all done — and whether he’s just Claude Code-d himself out of existence altogether. Have I even been texting with the real Kevin this week? WHO KNOWS.

Here’s Kevin’s homescreen, plus some info on the apps he uses and why:

The phone: iPhone 15 Pro (barely works, battery life is a joke, storage is full, but I’m holding out until I can preorder the Duo and become a new man).

The wallpaper: A photo of my son fishing at the Russian River.

The apps: Voice Memos, WhatsApp, Signal, Spotify, Google Maps, Safari, Day One, Brick, Stash, Superwhisper, Substack, Slack, Town, Apple Notes, Phone, Gmail, Messages.

I’m a big dictation guy, I barely type anymore, and I use Superwhisper and Voice Memos for everything. I vibe-coded a Pocket replacement called Stash that is still a delight many months later. (Building your own apps is so fun!) And I’m running a swarm of AI agents that includes Skynet (my ChatGPT Dot, which I use mostly for personal tasks), Hootie (my work agent, which runs on an app called Town that Casey got me into), and Nancy (my Muse agent, who trades Kalshi on my behalf and has lost me $41 to date).

I have a “red flags” app folder for social media and everything else I know is rotting my brain, a “green flags” folder for things that feel vaguely enriching, and an AI folder for all of my silly little bots.

I also asked Kevin to share a few things he’s into right now. Here’s what he sent back:

I’m hopelessly addicted to Balatro, a poker roguelike game that Casey got me into. (I will never forgive him for this.)

We’re starting a new, YouTube-first podcast, so I’m watching a lot of popular YouTube shows like New Heights and Good Work to get ideas.

For fun, I usually stick with my hobby channels: Served (a tennis podcast hosted by Andy Roddick) and Roffle Lite (a Balatro streamer whose videos I sometimes fall asleep to), plus some stuff my son likes (Mark Rober, Bluey, Yoto stories) that I’ve also gotten into.

My favorite new app right now is Dreambeans, a truly demented Google Labs app that sends AI-generated illustrations of personalized suggestions for things to do every day. I’ll open it up and it’s like, “Today you could go birdwatching at Point Reyes” and it’s just a stylized cartoon of me looking at a heron through binoculars. I don’t think people know Dreambeans exists but I love it and am preemptively sad for 6 months from now when Google shuts it down.

Crowdsourced

Here’s what the Installer community is into this week. I want to know what you’re into right now as well! Email installer@theverge.com or message me on Signal — @davidpierce.11 — with your recommendations for anything and everything, and we’ll feature some of our favorites here every week. For even more great recommendations, check out the replies to this post on Threads and this post on Bluesky.

“I’ve been using the markdown writing app, Em. I’m a longtime fan of iA Writer, but this plays so nicely with Ghost that my head has been turned.” — Chris

“Just got my Bose Wired Earbuds, and I haven’t felt this excited and happy for a pair of earbuds since AirPods.” — Sai

“I’ve been liking the app Shelf & Story for finding good books for my kids. Goodreads never quite cut it for me for that.” — Martha

“Made by the founder of TV Time, Bingers is my new favorite media tracker. Lots of really neat features (like easily updating dates and automatically populating a watchlist). Still can be improved but it’s off to a great start and is the first thing I reach for over Letterboxd these days.” — pegasusisme

“Just finished the most recent season of Jet Lag: The Game. Probably their best one yet. A fantastic jumping on point for anyone new to it.” — Shane

“Carrie, as soon as my internet provider resolves the outage affecting my area.” — Kev

“Doing my annual listen to Snow Crash — very much worth picking up in current times for anybody who has or hasn’t had the pleasure (Jonathan David is a PLEASURE to listen to).” — Jonathan

“Still playingFire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave. Completed my first path. Just in time for the expansion pass to get announced.” — Connor

“I’ve been really hooked on small roguelikes, like the city-builder meets Balatro in Combolands and the same twist but billiards in Ultrapool. I’ve been playing them on the Steam Deck which is good with some mouse tweaks, but you need to be comfy with the trackpads.” — Scott

Signing off

I mentioned last week that I’ve switched notes app, this time to Capacities. Again. A few of you asked what finally clicked for me, and the answer is really simple: Capacities has this concept of “objects” instead of “notes,” which treats everything you save as a discrete type of thing. Images get treated and categorized one way; PDFs another; text notes another. Everything lives on its own, but is also organized by tags, dates, and however else you want. Getting this setup right is a lot of work, because you have to create and tune each object the way you want, but I spent an afternoon watching football and entering metadata and suddenly I can find things in my notes app again.

This system won’t be for everybody — even at its best it’s pretty fiddly — but if you do wind up mucking around in Capacities, stare long and hard at this page in the documentation first. It’ll help.

See you next week!

fullText:
We broke the news this week that a next-gen Google TV Streamer is incoming, but it also arrives as Google’s smart home hardware strategy faces a tough spot and new competition.

9to5Google Weekender by Ben Schoon is a part of our free newsletter that also includes ‘Inbox,’ a twice-weekly roundup of key stories from around the web by Daniel Bader. Sign up here to get Weekender delivered to your inbox every Sunday along with ‘Inbox’ on Tuesday and Thursday. You can find past issues here.

Google’s smart home efforts have been a bit sporadic over the years. 2021 seemed like a turning point as the company rebooted its Nest camera lineup, but it was followed by a good bout of silence. That was broken up by the occasional new camera, streaming device, and the Google Home Speaker earlier this year, but it’s all felt rather unfocused and unpredictable.

And that leads into this week’s news: Google has a new TV Streamer coming.

	

This next-gen release is pretty similar on paper, though with the additions of far-field microphones, presence sensing, and a new remote. 

Next-gen Google TV Streamer in the works with microphones, presence sensing, & new remote

Sounds good! 

But, at the same time, it feels like Google should have much bigger priorities in its smart home ecosystem. Those aforementioned 2021 Nest cameras are still in need of refreshes. The 2K updates for the wired cameras have been welcome upgrades, but I do wish my battery-powered models had the same quality. The Nest Hub Max is way overdue for an update at this point, and I’d argue that should have been the priority over a new audio speaker. Google Home has done a great job over the past couple of years at building out a third-party ecosystem of smart home devices, but the first-party hardware has been lacking, and there’s not enough tight integration with most third-party hardware to bridge the gap.

So while I’m all for a new Google TV Streamer, I’m also struggling to feel like this is the release we should be seeing right now. 

Especially in the context of this week’s other news. Apple is making a big smart home play. On top of the “HomePad” smart display, the company is teaming up with LG for some second-party hardware with deep integration. Putting aside that Google has really dropped the ball on its massive lead in the smart display space, integrations like these are exactly what I wish Google Home saw more of. Walmart cameras, the Yale smart lock, and the First Alert smoke alarms are a good start, but there’s so much room for more.

As a fan and a genuine user of Google’s smart home ecosystem, I really feel like Google is leaving so much out there right now. Just me? Let’s discuss!

title: Google Antigravity is now built into Gemini app for macOS
snippet: As part of today’s Gemini 4 Argon rollout, Google is making a big update to the Gemini app for macOS by integrating Antigravity. more…
fullText:
As part of today’s Gemini 4 Argon rollout, Google is making a big update to the Gemini app for macOS by integrating Antigravity.

Antigravity is Google’s agent-first development platform, with version 2.0 introduced at I/O 2026. It was previously a standalone app for Mac, Windows, Linux, and most recently Googlebook (Android). Since May, Google has been updating Antigravity at a rapid pace, with major updates coming on a weekly basis, or even every few days.

Google is now bringing Antigravity directly into the Gemini app on macOS. You’ll see a new Liquid Glass pill for Antigravity in the top-right corner, with the same button letting you exit. This launches the full experience found in the dedicated application.

Gemini 4 Argon’s upgraded coding capabilities are cited as the reason for this integration. This lets users code apps, web experiences, and more from one app. As of today, the new model requires AI Pro and above in the Gemini app, but Antigravity access requires AI Ultra.

	

Meanwhile, the Gemini app for macOS has been updated with the new “Chat” and “Task” switcher, with the latter being the new name for Gemini Spark. It appears below the prompt box, while the navigation drawer also sees a big update. Search is now in the top-right corner of the panel. There’s a new Scheduled view that shows both Spark tasks and Scheduled actions.

Additionally, @ (mention) is now how you access Skills, replacing the / (slash) command. In the side panel, “Customize” lets you access Skills and Connectors, which is the new name for Connected Apps.

Make sure you’re running the latest version of the Gemini app for macOS.

title: Replit is no longer working with Anthropic, CEO says
snippet: Masad said the decision was made for a number of different reasons, including cost. Replit announced a partnership with OpenAI in August, but there was never any indication that it was no longer with Anthropic.
fullText:
Replit, the AI coding platform that has become a favorite of startup founders and developers, is no longer working with Anthropic, the company’s CEO and co-founder Amjad Masad said Thursday while onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt.

Masad said the decision was made for a number of different reasons, including cost. Replit announced a partnership with OpenAI in August, but there was never any indication that it was no longer with Anthropic.

“I think ChatGPT is better now,” Masad said, adding that the company uses an internal benchmark to help assess metrics like performance. “We publish a public benchmark as well, and consistently, Sol and Astra perform better on building vibe-coded applications from scratch. It was a decision based on both cost, partnership, and performance. And for all these reasons, we just felt like they were a better partner for now.”

Replit sells a cloud-based software development platform where users can develop and deploy apps directly from inside their browser. Under its partnership with Anthropic, Replit used the AI lab’s Claude models to run its platform. That partnership was said to have helped the company grow its revenue significantly.

Masad’s comments were rejected by insiders familiar with the partnership between the Anthropic and Replit, however. One person familiar, who asked not to be named, said the partnership was still in place.

There is evidence on the company’s website, blog posts, and social media posts that Replit was using Anthropic products as recently as a few weeks ago. For instance, a blog post in late September cites Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5 and Claude Fable 5.1 as models running in Replit Agent’s production environment. Around the same time, one of Replit’s product employees posted on X about using Anthropic’s flagship model Opus 5.5 and promoting its capabilities. 

TechCrunch reached back out to Replit for clarification and will update this story if we hear back.

Masad shared insights about the company’s growth while onstage at Disrupt, noting that enterprise is starting to provide a larger slice of revenue.

“We’re not sharing ARR numbers just yet, but in terms of growth, like, I would say, enterprise was like 2% of revenue last year,” Masad said. “This year, I would say like 15% of our revenue is enterprise contracts, and more than 50% of our revenue is B2B.”

Masad also commented on the necessity for good AI safety measures. 

“In the same way that us humans need a certain environment to work — you need a nice office, maybe nice good food in the office, air-conditioning, computer — agents need a habitat for them to exist and do good work,” he said. “So that habitat has good orchestration, good error recovery, good safety and security and sandboxing, good networking, good identity and authorization. And once you figure all of that out, then you can deploy AI safely.”

This article was updated to article to include more context on Replit using Anthropic’s models.

title: Why the Apple Home Collection will accelerate smart home adoption
snippet: I think it’s sometimes easy for geeks to forget that we live in a tech bubble with our fellow geeks. Many of us here have been using smart home technology for more than a decade now, some even for many decades. I’ve seen a lot of bemused comments on the Apple Home Collection, with people asking why anyone would want to pay significantly higher prices for devices which don’t seem to offer any added benefit. But I think this is absolutely a bubble effect … more…
fullText:
I think it’s sometimes easy for geeks to forget that we live in a tech bubble with our fellow geeks. Many of us here have been using smart home technology for more than a decade now, some even for many decades.

I’ve seen a lot of bemused comments on the Apple Home Collection, with people asking why anyone would want to pay significantly higher prices for devices which don’t seem to offer any added benefit. But I think this is absolutely a bubble effect …

HomeKit was a start, but not enough

In the very early days, smart home technology involved a great deal of soldering and programming. The tech gradually grew more accessible and fully wireless devices controlled by smartphones was the first major step change. All the same, configuring new devices was far from trivial, initially requiring a whole bunch of companion apps for products made by different manufacturers.

Apple’s attempt to change all this was HomeKit. The idea was that everything could be configured and controlled via a single app, with the HomeKit label guaranteeing compatibility. It also brought voice control to devices which previously required us to use an app.

The reality was still rather different from the vision, however. Some HomeKit devices still needed to be initially configured using a third-party app before they would appear in Apple’s Home app. Some of the setup processes made me feel like an unpaid network engineer.

Additionally, relatively few manufacturers bothered to make HomeKit-compatible products. Both the Amazon Alexa and Google Home ecosystems were far more commercially successful.

Matter and Thread helped

The launch of the Matter and Thread standards helped significantly. It meant manufacturers only had to support these new industry standards in order to ensure compatibility with each of the three big smart home ecosystems.

Matter also enabled a simpler setup process, again helping to make the technology more accessible to the mass market. Once more, however, the practical impact was limited.

Apple Home Collection

Many techies have been wondering what all the fuss is about with the Apple Home Collection. There are no new product categories, and there are equivalent but lower-cost options for each of the new devices.

	

But for non-geeks, the setup process really is completely different. Essentially, Apple has made configuring one of these devices as simple as pairing a new set of AirPods. Just like AirPods, you need only bring one of the new devices close to your iPhone, with CNET’s Ajay Kumar commenting on just how simple it appears to be.

I watched an Apple representative instantly find, pair and register a new smart home device on both her phone and the HomeView as she carried on a casual conversation with me, not missing a beat. Everything was managed through the Apple Home app. It seemed to work like pairing new AirPods or a HomePod. I didn’t have time to dig into the process before being shepherded to the next demo, but what I saw was one of the most compelling things I’ve seen in the smart home world: an easy, intuitive setup.

We shouldn’t underestimate just what a big difference this will make to normal people. I have definitely had non-tech friends be impressed by my smart home, but none of them rushed out to emulate it. I really do think this is going to represent the next step in mass market adoption.

If you’re a normie who likes the idea of a smart home but has been put off by the apparent complexity, I think we may now have reached the point where many are willing to make the leap.

That’s my view; how about yours? Please share your thoughts in the comments.

fullText:
The monthly “Google System Release Notes” primarily detail what’s new in Play services, Play Store, and Play system update across Android phones/tablets, Wear OS, Google/Android TV, Auto, and PC. Some features apply to end users, while others are aimed at developers.

The following first-party apps comprise the “Google System”:

Android AICore: Search the “All apps” list in Settings and open App info for the version number

Adaptive Connectivity Services: App info

Android Developer Verifier: App info

Android Pulse: App info

Android System Intelligence: App info

Android System Key Verifier: App info

Android System SafetyCore: App info

Android System WebView: App info

Android TV Core Services

Device Health Services: App info

Google Partner Setup: App info

Google Play Protect Service: App info

Google Play services: App info

Google Play Services for AR: App info

Google Play Store: App info

Google Play system update: Settings > About phone > Android version

Private Compute Services: App info

Quick Share Extension: App info

Search Engine Selector: App info

Settings Services: App info

SIM Manager: App info

System parental controls: App info

To update, open the Settings app > tap your name at the very top for “Google services” (on Pixel) > All services tab > Privacy & security > System services.

A feature appearing in the changelog does not mean it’s widely available. Some capabilities take months to fully launch.

	

Google Play services v26.40 (2026-10-12)

Device Connectivity

[PC] This update disables installation of the Find Hub app and removes Find Hub capabilities on Aluminium (Googlebook) devices.

System Management

[Auto, PC, Phone, TV, Wear] Updates to system management services that improve Updatability.

[Auto, PC, Phone, TV, Wear] Updates to system management services that improve Device Connectivity, Device Performance, and Stability.

title: Google Play adding ‘personal library’ to access your vibe-coded Android apps
snippet: Google today announced a slew of Play Store updates across vibe-coding, game discovery, social features, and more. more…
fullText:
Google today announced a slew of Play Store updates across vibe-coding, game discovery, social features, and more.

The biggest update is Google Play’s embrace of vibe-coded Android apps. Since May, Google AI Studio has allowed you to generate Android apps and quickly deploy them to your phone using ADB.

Google is now going a step further by letting you “launch personal apps on your own device” via the Play Store. A “Your personal library” section allows you to access apps across multiple devices for an easy restore and install experience. This is rolling out starting today in the US and other select markets.

The Play Store will soon let you privately share your apps with select users. These generated Android apps are kept “secure, private, and separate from the public store catalog.” It’s intended for small-scale sharing, with these apps going through a security review.

	

In the future, Google Play will let you “graduate to a professional developer account with the same Trust & Safety reviews and high-quality standards.”

Game Finder is the next big update and starts with your “Gamer DNA.” This is an “analysis of how you play and preferences you’ve shared.” You can specify “games, genres, mechanics, and more to finetune.” Gamer DNA will let you “easily find games that match your taste.” It’s rolling out initially in the US with more markets coming soon.

Plus, see how players with similar Gamer DNA are engaging with a title, find out how many people you follow are playing it, read user review summaries and learn which games are trending and why. 

This will be joined by Game Playlists that let you curate and soon share a collection of titles.

The Play Store is boosting social competitions with Sprints, or “high-energy, 48-hour micro-challenges” that involve matching with groups of two to five players for “fast-paced contests.” The Sidekick in-game overlay is also adding “30-second Playback” clips for sharing.

Elsewhere, Google Play is expanding Sports Topic Pages that show live scores and compatible streaming apps to the Premier League, Champions League, La Liga, Liga MX, and Major League Soccer. Ask Play can now generate app comparisons that highlight “key differences and user sentiment.”

title: New Apple TV 4K vs previous model: Here’s everything new
snippet: Apple just launched a brand new Apple TV 4K (pre-order here), the fourth generation of the product. Here’s how the new Apple TV 4K compares to the previous, third-gen model from 2022. more…
fullText:
Apple just launched a brand new Apple TV 4K (pre-order here), the fourth generation of the product. Here’s how the new Apple TV 4K compares to the previous, third-gen model from 2022.

Performance: A19 chip vs A15 Bionic

The new Apple TV 4K has an A19 chip, the same chip that debuted in the iPhone 17 last year.

The third-gen Apple TV 4K from 2022 includes an A15 Bionic chip that first shipped in 2021. So any sort of chip upgrade would have been a big one, but A19 is an especially sizable leap with several years worth of improvements.

Apple says the new chip “delivers up to 50 percent faster CPU performance and up to 2x faster GPU performance,” which results in “greater responsiveness, faster navigation, and smoother animations.”

A19 also has a new, dedicated AV1 decoder which enables “more efficient, high-quality streaming while using less bandwidth.”

Siri AI, plus hands-free Siri interactions with far-field mics

Siri AI debuts in the new Apple TV 4K, but Apple says it’s also coming to the second and third generation models. Presumably Siri AI will be more responsive on the latest hardware with A19, but it’s great that users won’t have to upgrade just to get the new Siri.

Apple says Siri AI supports features like “personal context understanding, broad world knowledge, and the ability to take even more systemwide app actions.” Some example queries include:

“What Apple TV shows won at the Emmy Awards this year?”

“Where was Pluribus filmed?”

“Is this appropriate for a 15-year-old?”

“Play the show Alinda recommended.”

One exclusive upgrade with the fourth-gen Apple TV 4K is that it includes a three-microphone array with voice isolation built right into the box itself for hands-free interactions.

This enables you to say “Siri” or “Hey Siri” to interact with the assistant. You’ll no longer have to press the button on the Siri Remote, though that’s still an option too.

Upgraded Siri Remote with Precision Finding

The Siri Remote has been upgraded to include Find My support with Precision Finding. 

If you’ve ever used Precision Finding to locate a lost AirTag or another device, you’ll know how valuable this experience should prove for the Siri Remote.

When you lose the Siri Remote, you’ll be able to get guided, step-by-step directions to its location. And thanks to a new built-in speaker, you can even play a sound on the remote to help you find it.

You can order the new Siri Remote here for $59, it’s compatible with older Apple TV 4K models so you won’t have to buy a whole new Apple TV to get it.

New four-speaker surround sound feature with HomePods

If you have several HomePods in your house, or plan to invest deeply in the Apple Home ecosystem, the fourth-gen Apple TV 4K has a new surround sound feature.

Using either HomePod mini 2 or HomePod 2, Apple TV 4K will support a four-speaker surround sound experience. Apple says, “The four speakers work together with Apple TV 4K to intelligently recognize their position in the room so audio timing and levels are automatically calibrated to the space.”

You can also mix and match HomePods, as long as they’re in matching pairs. For example, you can use a HomePod 2 front pair and a HomePod mini 2 rear pair—or opt for four of the same model.

Internal storage: 128GB standard vs 64GB

Apple used to sell Apple TV 4K in two models: one with 64GB storage and a more expensive 128GB model.

With the fourth-gen Apple TV 4K, 128GB is the standard storage configuration. There are no options to pay more for higher storage. It’s still unclear how necessary the extra storage is, but perhaps we’ll see tvOS 27’s Smart Downloads feature resurface soon.

Connectivity upgrades

There are several connectivity improvements with the new Apple TV 4K. On the wireless front, you get the following:

Wi‑Fi 7, up from Wi-Fi 6

Bluetooth 6, up from Bluetooth 5.0

Thread (previously limited to 128GB model)

	

It’s expected that these upgrades are due to the inclusion of Apple’s N1 wireless chip, though that hasn’t officially been confirmed.

Additionally, Gigabit Ethernet is now included standard on all models. Previously, it was excluded from the base 64GB model that most people bought.

New Apple TV 4K is now available for pre-order for $299.

fullText:
Following T-Mobile and Deutsche Telekom, Verizon has now confirmed how much it will charge customers to use Apple’s new iPhone Handoff feature. Here are the details.

Verizon customers to pay $10/month for iPhone Handoff

During Apple’s “Surprise and Shine” event last month, the company shared more details about iPhone Handoff, a new iOS 27 feature first previewed at WWDC that lets users share a single phone number across two iPhones.

Apple announced that the feature would initially be supported by T-Mobile and Deutsche Telekom, with Verizon and EE expected to follow before the end of the year.

Shortly after the event, T-Mobile confirmed a $5 monthly fee for iPhone Handoff, while Deutsche Telekom made the feature available through its existing MultiSIM service, which costs €6.95 per month unless already included in the customer’s plan.

Today, as spotted by MacRumors, Verizon also confirmed its pricing for iPhone Handoff, announcing that it will charge $10 per month, twice as much as T-Mobile.

Here’s Verizon:

Verizon will support iPhone Handoff, giving customers the flexibility to use a single Verizon phone number seamlessly across two compatible iPhone models. Whether using the pocketable iPhone Duo on the go or iPhone 18 Pro for work, customers can switch active status between devices at any time while keeping full access to Verizon’s 5G network. iPhone Handoff will be available from Verizon for $10/month on compatible iPhones models running iOS 27.

AT&T, meanwhile, seemingly has no plans to support Apple’s new iPhone Handoff feature. When CNET asked about it last month, the carrier acknowledged its potential benefits but said it was focused on its existing eSIM activation and transfer options instead.

title: Report: Apple’s antitrust negotiations with the DOJ spark concerns of a weak settlement
snippet: The Information reports that PayPal and Epic Games are among the developers concerned that a potential antitrust settlement between Apple and the DOJ might not go far enough in addressing the company’s allegedly anticompetitive practices. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
The Information reports that PayPal and Epic Games are among the developers concerned that a potential antitrust settlement between Apple and the DOJ might not go far enough in addressing the company’s allegedly anticompetitive practices. Here are the details.

A bit of context

A few months ago, Bloomberg reported that Apple and the DOJ were in talks to settle a 2024 antitrust lawsuit alleging that the company illegally monopolized the US smartphone market at the expense of consumers, developers, and competitors.

When the DOJ first filed the lawsuit, Apple pledged to “vigorously” defend itself and has continued to push back against the government’s allegations ever since.

Despite Bloomberg’s report about settlement talks, the case has continued to move forward, with Apple and the DOJ recently clashing over access to internal documents from federal agencies during discovery.

However, as The Information reported today, settlement talks have also continued behind the scenes, with the Justice Department apparently prioritizing iPhone interoperability.

Settlement talks advance

According to the report, the “department appears to be focusing on a deal addressing interoperability issues developers face with the iPhone,” although developers are concerned that any resulting settlement might impose only limited restrictions on Apple’s practices.

From the report:

As part of its talks with developers, the Justice Department has asked them for a list of ways to improve the iPhone’s ability to operate with other devices, the people said.

Many developers and antitrust lawyers are concerned that the Justice Department will oﬀer Apple a settlement that imposes relatively light requirements on how its devices interact with other companies’ devices.”

According to The Information, PayPal and Epic Games are among the developers that have directly raised concerns about a potential settlement with DOJ officials.

Meanwhile, some people involved in the settlement negotiations reportedly expected a resolution much sooner, although the pending Senate confirmation of Adam Candeub, Trump’s nominee to lead the DOJ’s antitrust division, could be contributing to the delay.

The report adds that Apple has changed some of its products and policies since the DOJ brought the lawsuit in 2024, including improving messaging interoperability with Android devices, but is likely to resist more substantial changes to its ecosystem, potentially complicating efforts to reach a settlement.

Asked about the discussions, a DOJ spokesperson declined to comment on the specifics, saying only that the department would “continue to prioritize affordability for all Americans across our economy.” Other companies mentioned in the report, including PayPal and Epic Games, declined to comment, while Apple didn’t respond.

title: Google’s Universal Cart puts a shopping cart everywhere, including Search homepage, Chrome
snippet: Yesterday, Google started rolling out its Universal Cart, and the company is very prominently placing it in Search, AI Mode, Chrome, and the Gemini app. more…
fullText:
Yesterday, Google started rolling out its Universal Cart, and the company is very prominently placing it in Search, AI Mode, Chrome, and the Gemini app.

This “intelligent shopping cart” was previewed in May at I/O 2026 as a “hub for shopping on Google.” It’s meant to help “organize your shopping, keep track of items you love from across retailers, stay on top of promos, and enjoy effortless checkout powered by the Universal Commerce Protocol.”

Universal Cart is now rolling out in the US, and we’re starting to see it in Google Search. A new shopping cart icon will appear in the top-right corner of google.com’s homepage and Search results, as well as on desktop Chrome’s New Tab Page. Clicking slides out a panel with two tabs for “Cart” and “My orders.” 

On mobile, the shopping cart appears to the left of the profile switcher in the Google app for Android. That icon also appears on the AI Mode homepage. 

	

In the Gemini app, “Cart and orders” now appears in the account menu.

This Universal Cart icon might be too prominent. It makes Google Search results that have nothing to do with purchases feel like a store page. This is incredibly jarring the first time you see it.

Google product pages gain an “Add to cart” button, with the Universal Cart letting you save products from multiple retailers. A pretty useful capability will automatically keep track of availability changes while offering price drop notifications. 

When you’re ready to purchase, Universal Cart will surface promo codes and highlight which payment method in Google Wallet will give you the most perks. Stores like Nike, Target, Walmart, and Shopify merchants will let you make purchases right from the Google interface.

title: iPhone Duo Preorders Sell Out in Minutes: Backordered Until January
snippet: Demand is strong for Apple’s first foldable, which will first be available on Oct. 23.
fullText:
The iPhone Duo, Apple’s first foldable phone, is a hot ticket. 

Preorders for the iPhone Duo began on Friday at 5 a.m. PT, on Apple’s website, the Apple Store app and elsewhere. Although the phone has an Oct. 23 release date, as of now models preordered through Apple won’t ship until the last week of January. The availability at mobile carriers like AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile is more variable. You can also try to buy one in stores on Oct. 23.

CNET Senior Tech Reporter Abrar Al Heeti got to handle the iPhone Duo briefly ahead of preorders, and described it as essentially a compact iPhone that can double as an iPad Mini, well suited for consuming media. Beyond that, she wrote, “It has a satisfying feel and really makes the crease virtually disappear when the screen is on.”

The 7.6-inch screen when opened is the largest iPhone display screen yet (there’s also a 5.4-inch outer display). The Duo is also equipped with two 48-megapixel cameras: a main camera and an ultrawide one.  It’s geared for multitasking, with Apple Pencil support and drag-and-drop functionality similar to an iPad. 

The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999, but trade-in offers and Apple’s Upgrade program could lower how much you pay out of pocket.

Apple is years late to the folding phone market, though that might not matter much to those already in the iPhone ecosystem. The bigger question is whether the iPhone Duo will be tempting to those inclined to buy Android phones, where the latest hinged options include the Samsung Galaxy Fold 8 and Galaxy Flip 8 and the Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold.
